test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A retailer permits a trade discount of 15%, followed by a cash discount of 20%, on an article. The net percentage of discount is :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net discount for **successive discounts** a% and b% is given by the formula: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Given **trade discount** a = 15% and **cash discount** b = 20%.

Net Discount = (15 + 20 − (15 × 20) ÷ 100)%.

Net Discount = (35 − 300 ÷ 100)% = (35 − 3)% = 32%.

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First discount = 15%, Second discount = 20%.

**Formulas:** Net Discount% = (Initial Price − Final Price) ÷ Initial Price × 100 | Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf557e5b4d758416419bd88ee0f75e12fa86d18538f339d46240b264a8d28a4d.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** of the article be 100.

⇒ After **15% trade discount**, Price = 100 − 15% of 100 = 85.

⇒ After **20% cash discount**, Selling Price (SP) = 85 − 20% of 85.

⇒ SP = 85 − (20 ÷ 100 × 85) = 85 − 17 = 68.

⇒ Net Discount = MP − SP = 100 − 68 = 32.

⇒ Net Discount percentage = (32 ÷ 100) × 100 = 32%.

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trade Discount vs Cash Discount

A **trade discount** is offered to all buyers in the same category, while a **cash discount** is provided to encourage immediate or early payment.

Successive Discounts

When more than one discount is offered on an article, they are calculated **consecutively**. The net percentage is always less than the simple sum of individual percentages.</p
